task:
Produce custom kubectl output using JSONPath and custom-columns.

Task A — Sort pods by creation timestamp:
  Write a kubectl command that lists ALL pods in ALL namespaces, sorted by creation timestamp.
  Save the command to /opt/course/5/find_pods.sh

  Command:
  kubectl get pods -A --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp

Task B — Sort pods by UID:
  Write a command to list all pods sorted by metadata.uid.
  Save to /opt/course/5/find_pods_uid.sh

  Command:
  kubectl get pods -A --sort-by=.metadata.uid

Task C — Custom columns output:
  Show pods with columns: NAME, NAMESPACE, IMAGE (first container image).
  Save to /opt/course/5/pod_images.sh

  Command:
  kubectl get pods -A -o custom-columns='NAME:.metadata.name,NAMESPACE:.metadata.namespace,IMAGE:.spec.containers[0].image'

Task D — JSONPath to extract specific fields:
  Get only the names of all Running pods in the default namespace.

  Command:
  kubectl get pods -n default -o jsonpath='{range .items[?(@.status.phase=="Running")]}{.metadata.name}{"\n"}{end}'

Create the /opt/course/5/ directory and all script files.
detailed_hints: For sort by creationTimestamp: kubectl get pods -A --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp
Combine with grep or filter: kubectl get pods -A -o jsonpath='{...}' | grep something

validators.description: kubectl get pods with sort works
JSONPath extraction works for pod names
